anchorsFit: There Will Be Blood: Daniel Plainview, the film is his psychology
Taxi Driver: Travis Bickle, seen from inside
Nightcrawler: Lou Bloom
Joker (2019): Arthur Fleck
Nayakan: Velu Naicker, a don the film understands without excusing
Guru: a tycoon who bends every rule and is still the film's heart
Mahaan: a man who chooses the empire over the family
anchorsMiss: Sivaji: The Boss and other mass-hero films: the lead breaks rules for a cause the film endorses; not an antihero
Batman Begins / Kill Bill: heroes on a mission, not studies of a wrong-doer
The Godfather: a family epic, prefer crime-grit-style (both can apply when the study is central)
Vertigo: obsession is the subject, prefer psychological-pressure-cooker
antihero-study.description: You leave having understood someone you would not want to be. The film studies a magnetic lead who does real wrong, and makes you feel the pull and the recoil at once.
qualifies: The protagonist commits real moral wrongs (not rule-breaking in a good cause), and the film stays inside their point of view instead of judging them from outside.
Character is the subject: the plot exists to reveal who this person is and what they become, and the ending measures the cost of being them.
The residue is empathy mixed with unease, not admiration. A hero with flaws, a vigilante the film cheers for, or a villain seen from the outside is not an antihero study.
antihero-study.title: Antihero Study

anchorsFit: Once Upon a Time in Hollywood: 1969 as a memory, with a rewritten ending
Jackie: grief as biography
Spencer: a fable from a true life
The Assassination of Jesse James by the Coward Robert Ford: myth-poetic history
Guru: Dhirubhai Ambani's rise as a melodrama with the names changed
anchorsMiss: Spotlight / 127 Hours: accurate reconstructions, prefer slow-burn-sharp-blade or one-room-pressure-cooker
The Social Network: the character study leads, prefer antihero-study
Bombay: a real event inside a fictional love story; emotional-gut-punch leads
based-on-vibes-true-story.description: You leave feeling the truth was emotional rather than literal. Rooted in real people or events, but the film cares more about tone, place and texture than about the record.
qualifies: The text says the film is based on, inspired by, or a dramatisation of real people or events.
The text or the film's reputation says it takes liberties: a fictionalised, loosely based, impressionistic or mythic treatment, not a procedural reconstruction.
The residue is a feeling about an era or a person, not knowledge of what happened.
based-on-vibes-true-story.title: Based on Vibes (True Story)

anchorsFit: Casablanca: the airport farewell
In the Mood for Love: the secret whispered into a wall
Before Sunset: the open ending
Past Lives: twenty-four years in one night
96: a reunion that ends at a door
Cast Away: the crossroads at the end
Thelma & Louise: defiance held in awe, so the residue is grace, not devastation
anchorsMiss: Manchester by the Sea / Hereditary: raw devastation, prefer emotional-gut-punch
The Shawshank Redemption / Rocky: the residue is hope and triumph, prefer rainy-day-rewinds
No Time to Die: one tragic ending inside a Bond film does not flip the register; prefer cat-and-mouse
Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara: warm and reflective, prefer rainy-day-rewinds
bittersweet-aftermath.description: You leave with a soft ache and a kind of gratitude. Something was lost or left behind, and the film treats the loss with grace, so the sadness comes mixed with beauty.
qualifies: The ending itself is a loss, a parting, a death accepted, or a road not taken, and the film treats it with grace rather than cruelty.
The residue is ache plus acceptance. If the ending wrecks you, use emotional-gut-punch; if it leaves you warm and smiling, use rainy-day-rewinds or feel-good-romance.
The ache is the dominant register of the whole film, not one sad scene inside a comedy, thriller or action film.
bittersweet-aftermath.title: Bittersweet Aftermath

anchorsFit: Mulholland Drive: identities dissolve across two halves
Memento: memory as structure, no time mechanics
Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind: erased memory from the inside
Coherence: realities swap over one dinner
Lucia: a pill that swaps dream and life
Persona: two psyches blur
anchorsMiss: The Sixth Sense / Fight Club / Shutter Island: one reveal reframes a stable film, prefer the-twist-is-the-plot
Rashomon: contradictory testimonies, but each is clear; prefer film-school-shelf and existential-core
Inception: the rules are explained; prefer heist-energy
Predestination: the time mechanics are the engine; prefer time-twists
brainmelt-zone.description: You leave reassembling the film in your head. Reality, memory or identity stayed unstable all the way through, and the pleasure was working out what you saw.
qualifies: The uncertainty is sustained across the film: unreliable memory, dream logic, doubles, shifting identities, contradictory realities. A single late reveal is the-twist-is-the-plot instead.
The plot summary itself is hard to state in order, or the text says the film is open to interpretation.
The residue is puzzlement that you enjoy, not fear (horror-and-unease) and not gentle wrongness (uncanny-vibes).
brainmelt-zone.title: Brainmelt Zone

anchorsFit: Heat: Hanna and McCauley
The Silence of the Lambs: Clarice and Lecter, Clarice and Buffalo Bill
Vikram Vedha: a cop and a gangster taking turns with stories and traps
Thani Oruvan: a cop versus a scientist-industrialist, each reading the other
Catch Me If You Can: a con man and the agent who chases him for years
Dial M for Murder and Strangers on a Train: the plan, then the counter-plan
The Terminator: hunter and prey across one city
anchorsMiss: Star Wars, Attack of the Clones, Return of the Jedi: adventure and war, not a duel
Kill Bill: a revenge list, not two opponents trading moves
Get Out / Rear Window: suspense built on one side watching, prefer horror-and-unease or psychological-pressure-cooker
Mass-hero cop films: qualifies only when the villain answers every move; a hero cleaning up a threat is not a duel
cat-and-mouse.description: You leave remembering a duel. Two named opponents who each know the other is coming, trading traps, escapes and reversals until one of them loses.
qualifies: There are two specific opponents (a cop and a thief, a detective and a killer, a victim and a stalker), and each one acts on what the other does: pursuit, trap, counter-trap, reversal.
The duel is the spine of the film from the setup to the climax, not a hero-versus-villain plot that resolves in one final fight.
Adventure, war, superhero and ensemble action films are not cat-and-mouse unless the text shows two opponents taking turns through the whole runtime.
cat-and-mouse.title: Cat and Mouse

anchorsFit: Lady Bird: senior year and leaving home
Boyhood: twelve years of becoming
Moonlight: three ages of one identity
Premam: three loves across one man's youth
Spirited Away: a child finds her courage in a strange world
The 400 Blows: the template
Call Me by Your Name: one summer that changes him
anchorsMiss: O Kadhal Kanmani / Vinnaithaandi Varuvaayaa: adult romances, prefer feel-good-romance or bittersweet-aftermath
Batman Begins: an origin story, not an identity study
Dead Poets Society: the arc is a tragedy, prefer emotional-gut-punch
Pisaasu: a grieving adult and a ghost, prefer horror-and-unease
coming-of-age.description: You leave having watched someone become themselves. A child, teenager or young adult crosses the line into a new self through firsts, mistakes and hard-earned perspective.
qualifies: The protagonist is young (childhood through early twenties) and the arc is their growth: first love, leaving home, a loss of innocence, finding a vocation, breaking from family.
The growth is the spine of the film. A youth subplot inside a drama, a romance between adults, or a hero's origin story does not qualify.
The ending leaves a changed person, not a solved plot.
coming-of-age.title: Coming of Age

anchorsFit: Heat: cops and thieves at the same level
Goodfellas: the life, then the cost
City of God: a favela's crime economy
Vada Chennai: North Chennai's gangs across decades
Fargo: a polite surface over a bloody scheme
Oldboy: a revenge story soaked in a criminal underworld
Kaithi: one night inside a drug syndicate's reach
anchorsMiss: The Matrix / Get Out / The Terminator: no criminal world, prefer their own registers
James Bond, Batman, mission films: a hero versus criminals from outside, prefer cat-and-mouse
Bullet Train / 22 Jump Street: comedy wearing crime clothes, prefer ha-ha-ha
Strangers on a Train / Rear Window: suspense among ordinary people, prefer cat-and-mouse or psychological-pressure-cooker
crime-grit-style.description: You leave with the taste of an underworld. The film lives among criminals, cops on the take and the people they ruin, and shows the violence with style and with consequences.
qualifies: The film is set inside a criminal world (gangs, the mob, hustlers, hitmen, corrupt police, a city's crime economy) and spends most of its runtime there.
Violence has weight: it bruises, it costs, it is not cartoonish. The filmmaking is stylish and precise about the world's texture.
Films where a hero fights criminals from outside (spies, superheroes, soldiers, vigilantes), horror films and science fiction are not crime-grit-style, however much crime they contain.
crime-grit-style.title: Crime, Grit & Style

anchorsFit: The Big Lebowski: the canonical cult object
The Rocky Horror Picture Show: the midnight template
Donnie Darko: a flop that became a shrine
Monty Python and the Holy Grail: quoted for fifty years
Thamizh Padam: a Tamil spoof that became a cult object
Naduvula Konjam Pakkatha Kaanom: a small Tamil comedy with a devoted following
Soodhu Kavvum: a black comedy that grew a cult
anchorsMiss: Fight Club: cult and canon; both can apply, but the text must say cult
Parasite / Everything Everywhere All at Once: acclaimed hits, prefer modern-masterpieces
10 Things I Hate About You: beloved, not cult
cues: became a phenomenon on home video
cult-chaos.description: You leave quoting it, already planning a midnight screening. A film people know line by line and love partly for its rough edges.
qualifies: The reception or legacy text says it: cult following, cult classic, midnight screenings, fan rituals, a reputation that grew after a weak release.
The film is remembered for an irreplaceable weirdness, quotability or excess, not just for being popular.
A mainstream hit with a loyal fanbase is not cult unless the text calls it one.
cult-chaos.title: Cult Chaos

anchorsFit: Before Sunrise / Before Sunset: the walk is the film
12 Angry Men: a jury argues
My Dinner with Andre: one dinner
Glengarry Glen Ross: language as a weapon
The Breakfast Club: one Saturday of talking
Vikram Vedha: stories told as traps, the Vikram and Betal frame
anchorsMiss: Pulp Fiction: iconic talk, but set pieces drive it; prefer crime-grit-style and ensemble-mosaic
The Social Network: fast talk inside a plot of deals and betrayals, prefer antihero-study
Kadhal Desam and other college romances with songs: not dialogue-driven
dialogue-driven.description: You leave remembering what people said. Conversations carry the tension, the comedy or the revelation, and the best scenes are two people talking.
qualifies: Most of the runtime is conversation: a walk-and-talk, a dinner, an argument, an interrogation, a debate. Adaptations of stage plays usually qualify.
The reception praises the dialogue, the screenplay or the verbal sparring specifically.
Films with great lines but a plot driven by action, chases or set pieces do not qualify.
dialogue-driven.title: Dialogue-Driven

anchorsFit: Requiem for a Dream: no mercy
Manchester by the Sea: grief that never lifts
Grave of the Fireflies: the opening tells you, and it still destroys
Kannathil Muthamittal: a child's search for her mother ends in a war
Dil Se..: a love story that ends in an explosion
Night and Fog: thirty minutes of the camps
Incendies: the final reveal annihilates
anchorsMiss: Past Lives / Her / 96: ache with grace, prefer bittersweet-aftermath
Black Swan: the register is psychological dread, prefer psychological-pressure-cooker
Roja: a kidnapping with a happy ending, prefer feel-good-romance or regional-gems
Interstellar: the loss is redeemed, prefer existential-core
emotional-gut-punch.description: You leave wrecked. The film delivers a blow it does not soften, and you sit with it long after the credits.
qualifies: A death, loss, betrayal or injustice lands late in the film and the film refuses to console you: no graceful coda, no earned peace.
The reception uses words like devastating, harrowing, heartbreaking, shattering, or the plot itself makes the blow plain.
If the ending is sad but graceful, use bittersweet-aftermath. If the pain is dread rather than grief, use horror-and-unease.
emotional-gut-punch.title: Emotional Gut Punch

anchorsFit: Magnolia: one day across a city
Short Cuts: Altman's template
Pulp Fiction: chapters out of order
Babel: four countries, one gunshot
Aayitha Ezhuthu: three men on one bridge, three stories
Crash: strangers colliding
anchorsMiss: Heat / Ocean's Eleven: large casts around leads, prefer crime-grit-style or heist-energy
Minsara Kanavu: a love triangle, prefer feel-good-romance
The Avengers: a team on one plot
ensemble-mosaic.description: You leave remembering a pattern, not a protagonist. Several storylines and points of view interlock into one picture.
qualifies: The plot summary follows three or more separate storylines or lead characters with no single protagonist, and they cross, collide or rhyme.
The structure is the point: chapters, intercutting, a shared event seen from several sides.
A large cast around one or two leads (a heist crew, a superhero team, a war platoon) is not a mosaic.
ensemble-mosaic.title: Ensemble Mosaic

anchorsFit: Synecdoche, New York: a life as an unfinishable play
The Tree of Life: grace versus nature
2001: A Space Odyssey: evolution and the unknowable
Stalker: a room that grants your true wish
Her: what love and consciousness are
Everything Everywhere All at Once: nihilism answered with a bagel and a hug
The Truman Show: a man discovers his world is a set
anchorsMiss: Inception / The Matrix: ideas of reality inside action films; prefer heist-energy, brainmelt-zone or cat-and-mouse
Dune: politics and prophecy, prefer quiet-epics
Samsaram Adhu Minsaram: a family drama, prefer rainy-day-rewinds
cues: what it means to be human
existential-core.description: You leave asking what any of it is for. The film's real question is meaning, mortality, identity or free will, and it asks it on purpose.
qualifies: Characters or the film itself explicitly confront a big question: what is a life worth, what happens when we die, who am I, is anything real, is there a God.
The reception calls it philosophical, existential, metaphysical, a meditation on, or the plot is built around the question (a dying man, a created being, a loop that forces reflection).
Science fiction or fantasy with existential set dressing but an action register does not qualify.
existential-core.title: Existential Core

anchorsFit: Koyaanisqatsi: image and score, no story
Man with a Movie Camera: the form as the subject
Last Year at Marienbad: narrative dissolved
Enter the Void: sensation as cinema
Stalker: slow cinema at its most austere (also existential-core)
anchorsMiss: Mulholland Drive: a narrative, however strange, prefer brainmelt-zone
2001: A Space Odyssey: experimental passages inside a narrative, prefer visual-worship and film-school-shelf
Holy Motors: provocation with episodes, prefer wtf-did-i-watch
experimental-cinema.description: You leave having experienced form directly. Structure, sound or image pushed into new shapes; story is minimal, absent or secondary.
qualifies: The text describes the film as experimental, avant-garde, non-narrative, an essay film, structural, or as rejecting conventional narrative.
A plot summary is hard to write because there is little plot: the film is images, rhythms, sound or a formal device.
Weird narrative films still have a story; they belong in brainmelt-zone, uncanny-vibes or wtf-did-i-watch.
experimental-cinema.title: Experimental Cinema

anchorsFit: When Harry Met Sally: the template
About Time: time travel in service of a love
Amelie: joy as a method
Alaipayuthey: a secret marriage, a fight, a reunion
Siva Manasula Sakthi / Minnale: Tamil romantic comedies where the lovers win
Thiruchitrambalam: a friendship that turns into the right love
Notting Hill: a meet-cute that ends in a garden
anchorsMiss: Casablanca / The Notebook / Past Lives: graceful loss, prefer bittersweet-aftermath
Vinnaithaandi Varuvaayaa / 96: the lovers do not end up together, prefer bittersweet-aftermath
Erin Brockovich / Attack of the Clones: a romance subplot inside another kind of film; not a romance
Blue Valentine: a marriage dying, prefer emotional-gut-punch
feel-good-romance.description: You leave warmed. A love story is the spine, the lovers end up together or happy, and the film wants you to smile about it.
qualifies: The love story is the main plot, not a subplot inside a drama, a legal case or an action film.
The ending unites the lovers or leaves them happy. Tragic, open or ambivalent endings go to bittersweet-aftermath or emotional-gut-punch.
The dominant register is tenderness, chemistry and joy, including Indian romances with comedy and songs when love is the engine.
feel-good-romance.title: Feel-Good Romance

anchorsFit: Citizen Kane: the textbook
Rashomon: the structure every film school teaches
Seven Samurai: the template for the team-on-a-mission film
Psycho: the shower scene and the mid-film murder of the lead
12 Angry Men: the single-room drama
Persona: Bergman's essential
Pather Panchali: the founding work of Indian parallel cinema (also regional-gems)
Harakiri: the samurai film turned against its genre
anchorsMiss: It's a Wonderful Life / Home Alone / Rocky: beloved, but the text must speak of influence or canon, not only of popularity
Fargo / Pulp Fiction: 1990s canon with National Film Registry status; both can apply when the text says so
Thamizh Padam: a spoof of canon, not canon
film-school-shelf.description: You leave knowing you watched something the medium learned from. A form-defining work: the editing, the acting, the structure or the genre grammar that later films inherited.
qualifies: The text says it: one of the greatest films ever made, National Film Registry, Sight and Sound polls, Criterion, widely studied, influential, pioneered, defined the genre, a landmark of a movement (neorealism, New Wave, Golden Age Hollywood, Japanese classical cinema, Indian parallel cinema).
Usually released before 2000. Old and popular is not enough: the text must speak of influence or canon status, not just success.
For films from 2000 onward, prefer modern-masterpieces unless the text already treats the film as canon.
film-school-shelf.title: Film School Shelf

anchorsFit: Airplane! / The Naked Gun: joke machines
Monty Python and the Holy Grail: sketch logic as a feature
Superbad / 21 Jump Street: comedy engines throughout
Panchatanthiram / Thenali / Vasool Raja MBBS: Tamil comedies where the plot is the gag
Kolamavu Kokila: a dark comedy that stays a comedy
Kung Fu Hustle: physical comedy as a martial art
anchorsMiss: Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara: a warm road movie with laughs, prefer rainy-day-rewinds
Little Miss Sunshine: a melancholy dramedy, prefer bittersweet-aftermath
A Fistful of Dollars / Singam 2 / Who Am I?: action with comic beats, not comedies
The Lobster: deadpan satire, prefer uncanny-vibes (comedy can be a second tag only when reviews call it funny)
Parasite: a satire that turns bloody, prefer modern-masterpieces
ha-ha-ha.description: You leave having laughed, a lot. Comedy was the delivery mechanism from start to finish, not a seasoning on something else.
qualifies: The film is a comedy by genre and by reception: the plot summary reads as gags, misunderstandings, spoofs or comic set pieces, and reviews talk about laughs.
Comedy is the dominant register of the whole runtime. A dramedy, a road movie with laughs, an action film with a comic sidekick, a horror comedy or a masala film with a comedy track does not qualify.
If you cried more than you laughed, or the ending turns tragic, this is not the tag.
ha-ha-ha.title: Ha Ha Ha

anchorsFit: Ocean's Eleven: the modern template
Inception: a heist run inside dreams
The Handmaiden: a con that keeps changing owners
Mankatha: a cricket-betting robbery and its betrayals
Dog Day Afternoon: a robbery going wrong in real time
Reservoir Dogs: the aftermath of a job
Baby Driver: getaway driving as rhythm
anchorsMiss: North by Northwest / The Hangover: no planned job, prefer cat-and-mouse or ha-ha-ha
Thani Oruvan: a cop's investigation, prefer cat-and-mouse
Rogue One: a mission inside a war film
heist-energy.description: You leave buzzing on the plan. A job with roles, a clock and a scheme, and the pleasure of watching it meet reality.
qualifies: The plot is built around a planned job: a robbery, a con, a break-in, an escape, a kidnapping for money, a sting.
There is a plan with parts (a crew with roles, a timetable, a gadget, a double-cross), and the film spends real time on the mechanism.
A single robbery scene inside another kind of film, or a hero chasing thieves, is not heist energy.
heist-energy.title: Heist Energy

anchorsFit: Hereditary: grief weaponised
The Shining: a hotel as a monster
Rosemary's Baby: paranoia that turns out to be right
The Witch: slow religious dread
Get Out: social horror
Demonte Colony / Pisaasu: Tamil ghost stories built on dread
Bramayugam: a folk-horror chamber piece
anchorsMiss: Asuran / Drishyam 2 / Uriyadi: violent dramas and thrillers, not horror
Rear Window / Strangers on a Train: suspense, prefer cat-and-mouse or psychological-pressure-cooker
The Lobster: strange, not scary, prefer uncanny-vibes
The Terminator: a chase with a monster; cat-and-mouse leads, horror can be a second tag
horror-and-unease.description: You leave scared, or with dread still sitting beside you. Menace drives the film, whether it screams or whispers.
qualifies: The film is a horror film by genre, or its dominant mode is sustained dread: supernatural threat, a slasher, body horror, folk horror, a monster, an inescapable menace.
Reception talks about fear: terrifying, scary, frightening, unsettling, nightmarish.
Violent dramas, revenge films, crime thrillers and suspense films with a sane threat are not horror unless the text frames them as horror.
horror-and-unease.title: Horror & Unease

anchorsFit: Donnie Darko: a rabbit, a countdown, a bedroom
Coherence: one dinner party and a comet
Under the Skin: an alien learns what skin is for
The Lighthouse: two men and a lamp
A Ghost Story: a sheet with eyes, waiting
Enemy: a double and a spider
Primer: a garage and a box
anchorsMiss: Hereditary: wants you scared, prefer horror-and-unease
Solaris / Stalker: argue the question at length, prefer existential-core
Shutter Island: resolves its mystery, prefer the-twist-is-the-plot
late-night-mind-rattle.description: You leave unable to sleep, not from fear but from an idea you cannot put down. Hushed, strange, unresolved films that are best at one in the morning.
qualifies: A small, strange premise (a loop, a visitor, a signal, a door, a double) treated quietly, with a small cast and little spectacle.
The ending is ambiguous or unresolved and the text says the film lingers, haunts or invites interpretation.
The tone is eerie-thoughtful, between horror-and-unease (which wants you scared) and existential-core (which argues its question out loud).
late-night-mind-rattle.title: Late-Night Mind Rattle

anchorsFit: Le Samourai: the archetype
Drive: a driver who barely speaks
No Country for Old Men: Chigurh's silence
A Fistful of Dollars: the squint
Kaithi: an ex-convict driving a lorry through one night, saying almost nothing
Ghost Dog: The Way of the Samurai: a code as a life
anchorsMiss: Kaththi / Ghilli / Thuppakki: mass-hero films with speeches and songs, prefer cat-and-mouse or rainy-day-rewinds
John Wick: kinetic action first; can be a second tag
Taxi Driver: the mind unravels, prefer psychological-pressure-cooker or antihero-study
Tenet: plot over presence, prefer time-twists
men-with-vibes.description: You leave remembering how the lead carried himself. Few words, total competence, a coiled stillness that the film treats as the whole point.
qualifies: The lead is laconic by design: the text or reviews mention few lines, stoicism, silence, a code, or presence over dialogue.
The film builds scenes around posture, ritual and waiting, punctuated by sudden violence; the style is cool and controlled.
Commercial mass-hero films with punch dialogues, songs and crowd scenes are the opposite of this register, however stylish the hero.
men-with-vibes.title: Men With Vibes (and Guns)

anchorsFit: Parasite: Palme d'Or and Best Picture
No Country for Old Men: Best Picture and consensus
In the Mood for Love: top of the century lists
Everything Everywhere All at Once: Best Picture and a cultural landmark
There Will Be Blood: near-universal landmark status
Oldboy: Grand Prix at Cannes and a global reputation
Spirited Away: the Oscar and the Berlin Golden Bear
anchorsMiss: Star Wars, Rear Window, Fargo, Titanic, North by Northwest: before 2000, use film-school-shelf
The Dark Knight / Inception / Skyfall: huge and admired, but the text must call them landmarks, not just hits
One Battle After Another and other new releases: acclaim on release is not yet standing; qualify only on major prizes or the strongest consensus language
cues: widely regarded as one of the best films of
modern-masterpieces.description: You leave feeling the bar moved. A film from 2000 onward whose craft, ambition and reputation all line up, and whose standing the record confirms.
qualifies: Released in 2000 or later (check the year in Identity). Earlier films never qualify here; use film-school-shelf.

The text confirms the standing: Best Picture won or nominated, Palme d'Or, Golden Lion, Golden Bear, Grand Prix, universal acclaim, best-of-decade or best-of-century lists, a landmark of its national cinema.
Popular and well reviewed is not enough; blockbusters and franchise entries qualify only if the text itself calls them landmarks.
modern-masterpieces.title: Modern Masterpieces

anchorsFit: Chinatown: the modern noir template
Drive: neon noir as elegy
Blade Runner: rain, shadow and a dying replicant
Following: a Nolan noir shot on weekends
Blue Velvet: suburban moral fog
Nightcrawler: Los Angeles as decay
Vertigo: obsession in noir clothing (secondary)
anchorsMiss: Sin City: pastiche with crime-grit energy, prefer crime-grit-style
Vada Chennai / Heat: bruised and kinetic, prefer crime-grit-style
LA Confidential: both apply; let the text decide
obsidian-noir.description: You leave in a fatalistic mood. Shadows, desire, a doomed protagonist and a world where every choice tightens the trap.
qualifies: The text calls the film noir or neo-noir, or the elements are all there: a detective or a drifter, a femme fatale or a fatal desire, a scheme, betrayal, a downward spiral, night and shadow.
The tone is fatalistic and sensual rather than kinetic and bruised; crime-grit-style is the louder cousin.
A crime film with a hopeful or heroic ending is not noir.
obsidian-noir.title: Obsidian Noir

anchorsFit: 12 Angry Men: a jury room
Rope: one apartment, one party
Phone Booth: one booth, one sniper
127 Hours: one canyon
Locke: one car
The Breakfast Club: one Saturday in one library
Oththa Seruppu Size 7: one man in one interrogation room
Coherence: one house during a comet
anchorsMiss: The Shining: a hotel is huge, prefer horror-and-unease
I (2015) / Demonte Colony: scenes in a house inside a bigger film; not confined
Samsaram Adhu Minsaram: one household, but the film moves freely; prefer rainy-day-rewinds
one-room-pressure-cooker.description: You leave remembering the room. One confined space held the whole film, and the walls did the squeezing.
qualifies: The plot keeps the characters in one location for most of the runtime (a room, a house, a car, a phone booth, a lifeboat, a canyon, a jury room), and the text says so or the summary never leaves it.
The confinement creates the tension: logistics, power dynamics, running out of time or air.
If the protagonist's mind unravels more than the space confines, prefer psychological-pressure-cooker; both can apply.
one-room-pressure-cooker.title: One-Room Pressure Cooker

anchorsFit: Black Swan: a dancer splits in two
Repulsion: a flat and a mind both rotting
Vertigo: obsession rebuilt in a woman's clothes
Shutter Island: an investigation into the investigator
Taxi Driver: a mind under siege
Anniyan: three personalities, one body
Persona: two women blur
anchorsMiss: Pisaasu / Insidious: hauntings with sane protagonists, prefer horror-and-unease
In the Mood for Love: restraint, not unravelling, prefer bittersweet-aftermath
Ghajini: memory loss as a plot device inside a revenge film, prefer cat-and-mouse
12 Angry Men: the space squeezes, prefer one-room-pressure-cooker
psychological-pressure-cooker.description: You leave feeling the mind was the battlefield. Paranoia, obsession, delusion or gaslighting, seen from inside the person coming apart.
qualifies: The protagonist's perception or sanity unravels across the film: hallucinations, obsession, paranoia, a double, gaslighting, a breakdown, and the film stays close to that mind.
The threat is at least partly internal. A ghost, a killer or a kidnapping with a sane protagonist is horror-and-unease or cat-and-mouse.
The reception calls it psychological, a descent, a study of madness or obsession.
psychological-pressure-cooker.title: Psychological Pressure-Cooker

anchorsFit: Pather Panchali: a village childhood as an epic
Days of Heaven: wheat, fire and a love triangle
Roma: one year, one household, one city
The New World: history as a whisper
Kadaisi Vivasayi: the last farmer
Tokyo Story: a family crossing a country
anchorsMiss: Dune / Dune: Part Two / Lawrence of Arabia: loud and grand, prefer existential-core, visual-worship or modern-masterpieces
Interstellar: ambitious and loud, prefer time-twists or existential-core
Meiyazhagan / Kumki: small-scale dramas, prefer rainy-day-rewinds or bittersweet-aftermath
quiet-epics.description: You leave having felt immensity without noise. Years, landscapes, generations or history rendered with patience and intimacy.
qualifies: The scope is large (decades, a region, a war, a family across generations) and the delivery is restrained: long takes, little action, attention to land, work and weather.
The reception uses words like meditative, patient, intimate, lyrical, unhurried, sweeping yet quiet.
Loud epics (battles, spectacle, a driving score) are not quiet epics, however big.
quiet-epics.title: Quiet Epics

anchorsFit: Blade Runner / Blade Runner 2049: the canonical template
Drive: pink neon and a scorpion jacket
Chungking Express: Hong Kong neon melancholy
Only God Forgives: neon as bloodstain
Enter the Void: neon as hallucination
anchorsMiss: The Matrix: green code, not rain and neon
Collateral: night Los Angeles, but digital grey, not neon
Vada Chennai: a gritty palette, prefer crime-grit-style
rain-neon-aesthetic.description: You leave carrying an image: wet streets, neon signs, synth glow, a city at night humming with melancholy.
qualifies: The text describes the film's look: neon, rain-soaked streets, night cityscapes, a synth score, cyberpunk or Hong-Kong-at-night texture, and the look is a signature critics mention.
The aesthetic is primary: the film is remembered for the city at night more than for its plot.
A film with a few neon-lit scenes does not qualify; the signature has to be the whole surface.
rain-neon-aesthetic.title: Rain & Neon Aesthetic

anchorsFit: The Shawshank Redemption: hope as a method
Rocky / The Karate Kid: underdogs you cheer for every time
3 Idiots: laughs, friendship and a happy ending
Boss Engira Baskaran / Siva Manasula Sakthi: Tamil comfort films
Paddington 2: joy distilled
The Princess Bride: quotable warmth
Zindagi Na Milegi Dobara: three friends, a road and a warm goodbye
anchorsMiss: Hereditary / Requiem for a Dream: rewatched by some, never comforting
Manchester by the Sea: warmth is not the residue, prefer emotional-gut-punch
Little Miss Sunshine: warm with an ache; may carry bittersweet-aftermath too
Singam: an action masala, not a comfort film unless reviews call it one
rainy-day-rewinds.description: You leave smiling and already wanting to watch it again. Warmth, hope or comfort is what stays, whether the film is a cosy comedy or an underdog story with real stakes.
qualifies: The residue is warmth, hope or triumph, and the film is known as a rewatchable comfort film: reviews say feel-good, crowd-pleaser, heartwarming, charming, beloved, or the film is a famous rewatch.
Stakes can be real (prison, poverty, a boxing match) as long as the film is remembered for its warmth and its ending lifts you.
Films remembered for pain, dread or disturbance never qualify, even when they are rewatched.
rainy-day-rewinds.title: Rainy Day Rewinds

anchorsFit: Nayakan: in TIME's all-time 100 list
Pather Panchali: the founding work of Indian parallel cinema
Roja / Bombay / Kannathil Muthamittal: National Film Awards and a changed Tamil cinema
Asuran: a National Film Award for Dhanush and a Tamil landmark
Vada Chennai: a landmark Tamil gangster saga by reputation
Premam: a Malayalam phenomenon
Drishyam: the thriller every industry remade
Thamizh Padam / Soodhu Kavvum: Tamil cult classics with the record to show it
anchorsMiss: Rashomon / Oldboy / Parasite: not Indian, use film-school-shelf, modern-masterpieces or underseen-treasures
A Tamil masala film with no acclaim in the text: Indian origin alone is not enough
Thug Life / Jana Nayagan and other recent releases: wait for the record
cues: one of the best Tamil films
regional-gems.description: You leave having watched a standout of Indian cinema. Tamil, Malayalam, Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, Telugu or any other Indian language, with the record to prove its standing.
qualifies: The film is Indian: an Indian language, an Indian production, Indian cast and crew (check the Lead and the names). Korean, Iranian, Japanese or other world cinema never qualifies here; use underseen-treasures or film-school-shelf.

The text confirms a standout signal: National Film Award, Filmfare win, Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Toronto or Rotterdam selection, India's Oscar submission, a cult classic, a landmark of its language's cinema, widely regarded as one of the best Tamil or Indian films, a film that changed its industry.
Indian origin alone is not enough. A commercial hit with no acclaim language in the text does not qualify.
regional-gems.title: Regional Gems

anchorsFit: No Country for Old Men: tension as craft
There Will Be Blood: 160 minutes to I'm finished
High and Low: a kidnapping, then a manhunt in slow focus
Harakiri: a story told in a courtyard until the blades come out
Drishyam: a family's cover story tightening
A Separation: domestic tension to a moral reckoning
Chithha: a search that grips harder every minute
anchorsMiss: Phone Booth / Jaws: real-time or set-piece thrillers, prefer one-room-pressure-cooker or cat-and-mouse
Heat: an ensemble crime epic, prefer crime-grit-style
Stalker: slow without the blade, prefer existential-core or experimental-cinema
slow-burn-sharp-blade.description: You leave feeling the payoff was earned by patience. Tension accumulated in stillness, then one precise release.
qualifies: The film is deliberately paced for most of its runtime, with tension building through observation, procedure or restraint rather than set pieces.
There is a decisive release: a confrontation, a reveal, a violent act, a reckoning, usually late.
The reception uses words like slow-burn, simmering, methodical, patient, taut, restrained. Kinetic thrillers and real-time pressure films are not slow burns.
slow-burn-sharp-blade.title: Slow Burn, Sharp Blade

anchorsFit: The Sixth Sense: the canonical reveal
The Usual Suspects: the last five minutes
Psycho: the mother
Shutter Island: the investigator is the patient
Gone Girl: a mid-film pivot
Pizza (2012): the ghost story that was something else
Following: who was using whom
anchorsMiss: Mulholland Drive / Memento: unstable throughout, prefer brainmelt-zone
Predestination: the twist is the time loop, prefer time-twists (both can apply)
Spectre / Interstellar: reveals inside action films, not twist films
the-twist-is-the-plot.description: You leave replaying the whole film to find what you missed. One engineered reveal reframes everything before it.
qualifies: There is a single late reveal (an identity, a death, a lie, the true nature of the setting) that the plot summary names, and it rewrites the meaning of earlier scenes.
The film plants clues and misdirection on purpose; the reception talks about the twist, the ending, or watching it twice.
Sustained unreality throughout is brainmelt-zone; a time mechanic is time-twists; an ordinary surprising ending is not a twist film.
the-twist-is-the-plot.title: The Twist Is the Plot

anchorsFit: Groundhog Day: the canonical loop
Primer: a garage and a paradox
Predestination: loops within loops
Back to the Future: the template
Tenet: inversion as a mechanic
The Terminator / Terminator 2: a war fought through time travel
Interstellar: time dilation and a message through a bookshelf
Oh My Kadavule: a second-chance ticket that rewinds a life
anchorsMiss: Om Shanti Om: reincarnation, not time travel
Memento / Pulp Fiction: non-linear editing only, prefer brainmelt-zone or crime-grit-style
Everything Everywhere All at Once: a multiverse, not time; prefer existential-core and modern-masterpieces
Michael Madana Kama Rajan / Tamizh Padam 2: no mechanic at all
time-twists.description: You leave having played with time. Loops, travel, resets, inversion or paradoxes drive the plot.
qualifies: The plot summary names a literal time mechanic: time travel, a time loop, a reset, time dilation, inversion, messages across time, branching timelines created by travel.
The mechanic drives the plot, not just a prologue (a time-travel setup that becomes an ordinary chase still qualifies when the summary keeps returning to it).
Reincarnation, flashbacks, non-linear editing, parallel universes without time travel, and dreams are not time twists.
time-twists.title: Time Twists

anchorsFit: The Lobster: single people become animals
Dogtooth: a family's invented language
Upstream Color: dream logic as plot
Under the Skin: an alien in Glasgow
Being John Malkovich: a door on the seventh-and-a-half floor
The Truman Show: a town that is a set (secondary)
anchorsMiss: Midsommar / The Shining: crosses into horror, prefer horror-and-unease
Mulholland Drive: fractures perception, prefer brainmelt-zone
Spirited Away: a fantasy world with its own clear rules, prefer coming-of-age
Pizza / Insidious: ghost stories, prefer horror-and-unease
uncanny-vibes.description: You leave with a deja vu that will not shake. Reality was slightly off the whole time: rituals, deadpan rules, familiar places gone strange.
qualifies: The film's world runs on strange rules presented as normal: a dystopia with absurd laws, a family with invented words, a town that behaves wrongly, a deadpan surreal premise.
The strangeness is gentle and persistent rather than scary (horror-and-unease), puzzling (brainmelt-zone) or shocking (wtf-did-i-watch).
Reception uses words like surreal, deadpan, absurdist, off-kilter, dreamlike, strange, Kafkaesque, Lynchian.
uncanny-vibes.title: Uncanny Vibes

anchorsFit: The Fall: visual maximalism almost nobody saw
Coherence: a micro-budget gem
Timecrimes: a Spanish time-travel find
After Hours: a Scorsese flop that became a favourite
The Brand New Testament: a Belgian oddity
A Ghost Story: an indie most people missed
anchorsMiss: Parasite / Oldboy: world cinema with global fame, prefer modern-masterpieces
Soodhu Kavvum / Naduvula Konjam Pakkatha Kaanom: Indian, prefer regional-gems
Donnie Darko: a flop that became a cult object, prefer cult-chaos
underseen-treasures.description: You leave feeling you found something. A film that few people saw and more people should have: low visibility, high payoff.
qualifies: The text says the film was overlooked: a box-office failure, a limited release, underrated, underseen, little-seen, a sleeper, rediscovered, reappraised, a festival film that never found an audience.
The payoff is real: the same text praises it, or it later gained a reputation.
Famous films, big hits and mainstream award winners never qualify. Indian films with acclaim go to regional-gems instead.
underseen-treasures.title: Underseen Treasures

anchorsFit: Lost in Translation: a week in a hotel
Chungking Express: two stories that barely happen
Only God Forgives: a corridor and a song
A Ghost Story: time passing under a sheet
Columbus: buildings and two people
Paterson: a week of a bus driver's poems
anchorsMiss: Drive: a crime plot, prefer obsidian-noir or men-with-vibes
The Tree of Life: form-forward, prefer experimental-cinema or existential-core
Backrooms: dread with a thin plot, prefer horror-and-unease
vibe-is-the-plot.description: You leave having felt something rather than followed something. Mood, music, colour and pacing carried the film; the plot fits in a sentence.
qualifies: The plot summary is thin or episodic: people drift, meet, wander, wait. Little conflict drives the story.
The reception talks about atmosphere, mood, texture, music or feeling more than about story, and often calls the film a tone poem, hypnotic, dreamy or atmospheric.
A clear genre plot with strong style (a crime story, a thriller, a heist) is not vibe-is-the-plot; tag the genre bucket and add visual-worship if the look dominates.
vibe-is-the-plot.title: Vibe Is the Plot

anchorsFit: 2001: A Space Odyssey: image as metaphysics
In the Mood for Love: Christopher Doyle's frames
Blade Runner 2049: Deakins painting with light
The Fall: visual maximalism
Portrait of a Lady on Fire: painterly restraint
The Handmaiden: every room a composition
Kill Bill: Vol. 1: the House of Blue Leaves as choreography and colour
Stalker: the Zone as a sequence of paintings
anchorsMiss: Drive: obsidian-noir and men-with-vibes lead
The Grand Budapest Hotel: visual, but the register is ha-ha-ha
Backrooms: found-footage dread, prefer horror-and-unease
visual-worship.description: You leave remembering images. Frames composed like paintings, light and colour doing the storytelling, the eye engaged before anything else.
qualifies: The reception praises the cinematography, the compositions, the production design or the colour specifically: a Best Cinematography win or nomination, a named cinematographer singled out, visually stunning, every frame a painting.
The look is central to the film's reputation, not an incidental compliment in a review that is about something else.
Good-looking films with a stronger primary register get that register first; add this tag only when the images are what the text keeps returning to.
visual-worship.title: Visual Worship

anchorsFit: Holy Motors: the archetype
Titane: body horror as love story
The Substance: body-horror maximalism
Possession: a divorce as demonic opera
mother!: allegory as assault
Enemy: an ending nobody expects
anchorsMiss: Mulholland Drive: strange with intent, prefer brainmelt-zone
Everything Everywhere All at Once: chaos that resolves warmly, prefer modern-masterpieces
Saint Maud: dread, prefer horror-and-unease
The Lobster: deadpan rather than confrontational, prefer uncanny-vibes
wtf-did-i-watch.description: You leave stunned and a little delighted at the nerve of it. Transgressive, absurd or confrontational cinema that broke decorum on purpose.
qualifies: The text describes shock, transgression or provocation: body horror, graphic excess, taboo subjects, walkouts, divisive reactions, a notorious scene.
The film is remembered for daring you to keep watching, not for a puzzle (brainmelt-zone) or for gentle strangeness (uncanny-vibes).
Reception uses words like transgressive, provocative, grotesque, outrageous, divisive, confrontational, extreme.
wtf-did-i-watch.title: WTF Did I Watch
